components.summary: Blender 5.2.2 renders WalletWallaby. Blender's source is GNU GPL v2 or later, and GPL v3 or later is the license to use for any distribution of its binaries; it may be used commercially and for any purpose. This repository installs the official build, verified by the SHA-256 pinned in config/blender.json, and never redistributes it.

Remotion renders the video. Its license is the vendor's own source-available license, not an SPDX one: free for an individual, a for-profit organization with up to 3 employees (the installed 4.0.532 text), a non-profit, or evaluation; a company license otherwise. The vendor's Terms (labelled 5.0, not yet in effect) count the headcount of all personnel among the involved parties. This repository lives in a GitHub organization with several members; the project is currently developed and operated by the owner. Whether that qualifies for the Free License is an owner and vendor question. No paid license is claimed.

resolution.ownerAction: Confirm with the vendor, or obtain a company license, whether this project qualifies for the Free License (see the vendor's license FAQ); then record the outcome as this item's clearance. A GitHub organization member count is not a headcount and decides nothing by itself.
resolution.reassessmentTrigger: Any change to the pinned Remotion version (this check enforces it), Remotion 5.0 taking effect, a change in who develops or operates the project or in its team size, or a change to the vendor's terms.

Each is MIT, MIT or Apache-2.0, or Unlicense or MIT; MIT is elected throughout, and the copyright and permission notices ship in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. libm carries extra notices (musl, Sun Microsystems, and others), and Rust's own core and alloc libraries (MIT or Apache-2.0) are compiled in too. ElevenLabs synthesizes the narration (the publication binding in config/narration-providers.json). It is an external proprietary service under its Terms of Use (non-EEA edition, last updated 09 October 2026), not an open-source dependency; the Terms let paid plans use it commercially. The narration voice is a Voice Library Professional Voice Clone, as the owner reports (voiceRights.attestation); by the provider's rules only the person whose voice it is can create, verify, and publish such a clone for other users. WalletWall holds no ownership in the speaker's voice or likeness and claims only its authored script, composition, and audiovisual work. voiceRights keeps the right to use the voice apart from the right to use its output commercially, and records the provider controls as found. Read 2026-10-22: the Terms, the Prohibited Use Policy, the Voice Library Addendum, and the API and Creative terms. No credential, account identifier, or plan tier is recorded here, only that synthesis was on a paid plan.

attestation.basis: The owner inspected the voice in the provider's interface and reported it to the owner-rights clearance lane on 2026-10-22: a Professional Voice Clone, Australian English, narration, with a 30-day notice period. That it is its speaker's own verified clone, intentionally published for others, rests on the provider's rules for the Voice Library (only a verified owner can publish a clone), not on an independent check of who the speaker is. It cannot be re-read offline.

providerControls.note: The owner reported a 30-day notice period on the voice's Voice Library listing, read in the provider's interface (the provider's stated minimum is 30 days). A notice period governs how long a voice stays available after its owner withdraws it: users who saved it keep access for the period, and output generated before it ends continues to exist (Voice Library Addendum, section 4). It is a condition of availability, not a restriction on this use. Not verifiable offline.

Whether the voice's owner enabled Live Moderation was not read and cannot be read offline. When enabled, the provider screens each request's text against prohibited categories and may refuse a request or add latency; it changes no right in output already generated.

Whether the voice's owner set a restriction beyond the notice period and Live Moderation (for example excluding free-plan users, which the provider documents as an owner option) was not read and cannot be read offline. The Voice Library Addendum describes no other owner-set restriction, but the Terms make restrictions on the use of a User Voice Model that are disclosed within the Services part of the agreement, so one found in force binds this use. Record it here with the owner's compliance record before the voice stays CLEARED.

No withdrawal has been reported to this record, but whether the voice's owner later withdraws it, or the provider removes it (the Addendum reserves that right, with or without notice), cannot be determined offline. A withdrawal is prospective: it ends synthesis after its notice period and is no evidence that output generated while the voice was available was unauthorized.

clearance.basis: Recorded on the owner's instruction (owner-rights clearance lane, 2026-10-22) after the Terms, Prohibited Use Policy, Voice Library Addendum, and API and Creative terms were read that day. By the provider's rules a Professional Voice Clone is created and verified only by the person whose voice it is and published to the Voice Library only by that person, for other users; the provider authorizes its use and a paid plan carries a commercial license. The owner reports the voice is such a clone and states the narration set was generated through the owner's paid account. Reassess before each synthesis, on a change of plan or terms, and if the voice is withdrawn.

components.summary: The character frames: what Blender renders of the cleared model in a scene the lane builds from code (a flat world colour, one sun, the teaching or depth camera, the contact shadow, and declared terrain blocks), with no image loaded into it. They are the seven committed character reference frames (idle, crouch, airborne, landing, perch, inspect, tail-brace) and the character crops inside a release, which Remotion composites. Blender's license page says what you create with Blender is your sole property, and its FAQ that its output is program output and the user's; the GNU GPL FAQ says a program's license does not reach its output unless the output copies the program's own text or art. So the GPL on the eight Blender-API scripts says nothing about these frames. Frames that project a Remotion frame (the depth reveal) are not this item: they are blender-depth-reveal-output.

attestation.basis: The owner states, 2026-10-26, that WalletWall owns the composition and the character and assets it supplies to these renders, subject to third-party rights in the tools. The code shows this class: the job writers (scripts/blender-proof.ts, src/blender/production.ts) give a character job no image, and render.py and the lane modules it loads build its scene from code and load an image only for a depth reveal (transition.py), which is not this item. The record covers the rendered frames, not Blender (blender-runtime) or the GPL scripts. The lane's code carries no third-party code, and the seven reference frames are byte-identical to those attested on 2026-10-25.

components.summary: The depth-reveal frames: Blender's render of the lesson's 2D-to-3D transition, in which every pixel of text, card, and route is a Remotion frame (rendered characterless, with captions and the footer off) projected onto lane-built blocks and a paper sheet, with the character where it is in view (blender/walletwallaby/transition.py). They are the three committed transition reference frames (transition-entry, transition-peak, transition-exit) and the reveal frames inside a release. They incorporate Remotion's output, so they are not cleared before remotion-render-output is, whatever the Blender side establishes.

resolution.ownerAction: Resolve remotion-render-output (these frames carry Remotion's own frames as textures), then record this class's provenance and clear it.
resolution.reassessmentTrigger: The remotion-render-output item changes status, or the depth reveal stops projecting Remotion frames.

components.summary: The WalletWallaby .blend and its canonical model (BLENDER_CHARACTER in src/character/walletwallaby/versions.ts: model v2 2c92f3c3, materials v2 de8c55f5), generated by blender/walletwallaby/build.py from an empty factory scene. The body, limbs, ears, face, and claws are surface-nets meshes of signed-distance volumes whose placements and sizes the lane authors (geometry.py, and build.py for the ears, face, and claws); the contact shadow is a disc from Blender's built-in circle primitive; the armature is built from the rig contract; the materials are node trees in exact brand colours; and the one image, the belly's mortar map, is computed in materials.py and packed. Nothing is imported, downloaded, appended, or linked: no mesh, texture, rig, material library, model fragment, or reference asset, in the code or in its history. The .blend is data only, with no scripts, and is reopened with scripts disabled. Its signed-distance code is written in this repository from the definitions; until 2026-10-26 it was translated from Inigo Quilez's articles (the retired quilez-sdf-forms item, docs/LICENSING.md, "Signed-distance code").

attestation.basis: The owner states, 2026-10-26, that the canonical WalletWallaby model (v2) was created for WalletWall from repository-owned source. The code shows how it is made, as the summary sets out: build.py and the lane modules it loads generate every part of it, and none of them imports, downloads, or loads a mesh, texture, rig, material library, model fragment, or reference asset, now or in their history. The signed-distance code they run is written in this repository from its definitions and carries no third-party code; against v1 the model differs only by an enclosed shell removed from each eye glint and a sub-pixel change in the chin's tessellation.
